cards.b: ΔEp = mgΔh (g = 9.8 N/kg, Δh = change in height).
W = Fd = ΔE: force × distance moved in the direction of the force.
Work done per unit time or energy transferred per unit time: P = W ÷ t = ΔE ÷ t. Unit watt (1 W = 1 J/s).
Useful energy output ÷ total energy input (× 100%); or useful power output ÷ total power input (× 100%).
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred between stores; the total stays constant.

cards.f: Where does wasted energy usually end up?
cards.b: As internal (thermal) energy of the surroundings.
Kinetic, gravitational potential, chemical, elastic (strain), nuclear, electrostatic, internal (thermal).

cards.f: Describe the energy transfers for a braking car
cards.b: Kinetic energy → internal (thermal) energy of brakes and surroundings, by work done by friction.

cards.f: Steps in most thermal power stations
cards.b: Boiler (heats water to steam) → turbine → generator → electricity.
Wind: it turns the turbine directly. (Also hydroelectric, tidal, waves, solar cells.)

cards.f: Advantage and disadvantage of wind power
cards.b: Advantage: no fuel or emissions. Disadvantage: unreliable (wind varies) and small output per turbine.
Fission: splitting of a nucleus (reactors). Fusion: joining of nuclei (the Sun).

cards.f: Energy sources NOT originally from the Sun
Trap: holding a heavy box still
cards.b: No work is done on the box, because it does not move in the direction of the force.

short.q: A ball of mass 0.50 kg is dropped from a height of 20 m. Ignoring air resistance, calculate its speed just before hitting the ground. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
short.model: Loss in Ep = gain in Ek: mgh = ½mv², v = √(2 × 9.8 × 20) = 20 m/s.

short.q: A student of mass 60 kg climbs stairs 4.0 m high in 8.0 s. Calculate her power. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
A motor uses 500 J of electrical energy and lifts a load gaining 350 J of gravitational potential energy. Calculate the efficiency and state where the rest of the energy goes.
short.model: Efficiency = 350 ÷ 500 × 100% = 70%. The other 150 J is wasted as internal (thermal) energy (and sound).

short.q: Give two advantages and one disadvantage of using hydroelectric power.
short.model: Advantages: renewable, no fuel cost, reliable / can respond on demand. Disadvantage: floods valleys / destroys habitats / few suitable sites.
points: two advantages from renewable, reliable, no fuel cost, no CO₂ in operation
one disadvantage e.g. flooding, habitat loss, few sites

short.q: Describe the energy transfers when a stretched catapult fires a stone that then lands in the ground.
short.model: Elastic (strain) energy → kinetic energy of the stone (→ gravitational potential at the top) → kinetic energy → internal (thermal) energy of the ground and air when it stops.
